answers.5_blockers_for_PR_131_merge: None. The fix is exactly D-45(B), the gates are green, the mechanism is verified by five independent mutations each targeting a distinct load-bearing piece, the away case is preserved, the data is digit-free and under the cap, the audit assertion still passes on the Sol return (every number on the panel is still a binding), and nothing outside ui/ + data/news/ + tests/ was touched. The two minor observations below are non-blocking and the same code is already on draft PR #131 ready to merge per Mark's attended 2026-10-06 ruling.

minor_observations_non_blocking.note: build() still calls header.compose(NewsCopy.header_parts(copy, false)) with a hardcoded false. This is safe because show_world() recomposes with the correct flag immediately after, but it duplicates the (header_lead, epoch slot, header_mid, age slot, header_tail) intent literally in NewsCopy and then in the false-branch header_parts call. A future caller that uses build() without show_world() would render a stale 'already 0.00 years old.' header. Not blocking for this PR; a follow-up could have build() call header.compose(NewsCopy.header_parts(copy, false)) AND raise a one-line comment that show_world is the authoritative recompose.

body.no_age_text = labels["body_no_age"] runs in build() but the lint only verifies that the label is digit-free; it does not verify that the label is present. If the label is ever deleted from copy.json, the no-age body would be empty (mutation M5 demonstrates this). The mutation also shows the gate catches it, so the safety net is the test, not the lint. Not blocking for this PR; a follow-up lint check for label presence would be a tighter guarantee.
